Test: fossil age outliers

Source: R/test-docs.R
test_age_outlier.Rd

Flags fossil records whose age is far from the ages of the other records of their taxon. One age is drawn uniformly from each record's range (the minimum age when the range has zero width), each record gets its mean absolute age difference to all records of the taxon, and records above the upper fence (Q75 + mltpl x IQR, or median + mltpl x MAD) are outliers. The draw is repeated replicates times and a record is flagged when it is an outlier in more than 1 - flag_thresh of them. Taxa with fewer than size_thresh records are not tested.

Details

The draws are seeded per taxon from seed and the taxon name, and taken in an order fixed by the records' ages, coordinates and identifier, so the flags are reproducible and do not depend on the order or the splitting of the input. The caller's random-number stream is left unchanged.

Fields

min_age, max_age, species (the taxon), and lon, lat for uniq_loc.

Settings

settings = list(age_outlier = list(...)) with method ("quantile"), mltpl (5), size_thresh (7), replicates (5), flag_thresh (0.5), uniq_loc (FALSE: when TRUE, records sharing taxon, coordinates rounded to 0.1 degrees and ages are tested once) and seed (1).

CoordinateCleaner

Equivalent to cf_age() at taxon level; identical flags when no age has to be drawn (every range of zero width). Otherwise both draw ages at random and the flags agree in distribution, not record by record: CoordinateCleaner draws from the session's random stream in input order.

See also

flag_occurrences(), flag_tests()

Other tests: test_age_equal, test_age_range_outlier, test_aohi, test_basis, test_capital, test_centroid, test_country_mismatch, test_dataset_ddmm, test_dataset_rounded, test_duplicate, test_equal, test_establishment, test_gbif_headquarters, test_gbif_issue, test_institution, test_invalid, test_outlier, test_range, test_sea, test_spatiotemporal_outlier, test_urban, test_zero

Examples

x <- data.frame(accepted_name = "A", min_ma = c(rep(20, 20), 90), max_ma = c(rep(22, 20), 92))
flag_occurrences(x, tests = "age_outlier",
                 columns = occ_columns(species = "accepted_name"))$flag_age_outlier
